title: October and November are Texas' deadliest months for pedestrians, TxDOT warns
excerpt: As daylight saving time ends November 1 and nights grow longer, TxDOT says October and November see the highest number of pedestrian crashes in Texas.
content:
October and November are the months when pedestrian crashes are most likely in Texas, the Texas Department of Transportation warns, as daylight saving time ends November 1 and evenings grow darker earlier.

In 2025, 694 people were killed by vehicles in Texas while walking, and nearly 20 percent of those deaths happened in October and November, according to TxDOT. Those months had the highest number of pedestrian crashes all year.

Most of the danger comes at night: 68 percent of pedestrian fatalities and serious injuries in Texas last year occurred in the dark, TxDOT said. Pedestrian deaths still made up 18 percent of all traffic deaths in the state, even though pedestrian fatalities fell 10 percent from 2024.

TxDOT is asking drivers to watch for people walking and to drive like a Texan — kind, courteous and safe — under its Be Safe. Drive Smart. campaign, with street teams of walking billboards sharing pedestrian safety tips through October and November.

For Laredo and Webb County, the warning lands as the days shorten: drivers should slow down and stay alert near crosswalks and neighborhoods after dark, and people walking should stay visible and use crosswalks where they are available.

Sources:

  • Texas Department of Transportation, "As nights get longer, TxDOT reminds Texans to look out for people walking," October 2026
  • KGNS, "TxDOT: October and November are the most dangerous months for pedestrians," November 1, 2026
